The informational route, with conformity because others are better informed
The central route, with careful evaluation of the strength of the arguments

questions.prompt: A study asks volunteers to do a dull task and then tell the next person it was enjoyable. One group is paid $1 and another $20. Later, the $1 group rates the task as more enjoyable. Which explanation fits?
choices: The $20 group experienced overjustification and lost all interest in the task
The $1 group conformed to the majority in a normative influence situation
The $20 group displayed a self-serving bias that credited success to ability
The $1 group had insufficient external justification and shifted their attitude

questions.prompt: The reduced likelihood that any one person helps when others are present is the:
choices: Bystander effect, tied to diffusion of responsibility among observers
Social loafing effect, tied to lowered effort in a group task
Groupthink effect, tied to the suppression of dissenting opinions
Halo effect, tied to a general impression shaping specific judgments

questions.prompt: Which is an example of discrimination rather than prejudice?
choices: A landlord privately believes that families with children are noisy
A landlord refuses to rent to a family because of its ethnic background
A tenant assumes that landlords generally prefer older tenants
A tenant feels uneasy and anxious around people who are unfamiliar

questions.prompt: Which condition is NOT part of Allport contact hypothesis for reducing prejudice?
choices: Pursuit of shared goals through active cooperation between the groups
Support from authorities, law or custom for the contact between groups
Competition between the groups for scarce resources and rewards
Equal status between members of the groups who are in contact

questions.prompt: After a team reviews a case, each member leaves more extreme in the initial cautious view than before the meeting, and a junior member who disagreed said nothing. Which pairing of concepts best explains this?
choices: Deindividuation and the bystander effect, with a loss of self-awareness
Stereotype threat and the self-fulfilling prophecy, with impaired performance
Social facilitation and the mere exposure effect, with better performance
Group polarization and groupthink, with strengthened views and suppressed dissent

questions.prompt: A hospital sets a policy under which patients without a permanent address are never scheduled for follow-up, though no staff member holds any ill will toward them. Which concept does this best illustrate?
choices: Structural discrimination, unequal treatment built into policy and practice
Implicit bias, an automatic association operating outside of awareness
Stereotype threat, impaired performance that stems from awareness of a stereotype
Individual prejudice, a negative attitude held by an individual person

questions.prompt: Which sociological theory views society as a system of interdependent parts that each serve a function?
choices: Rational choice theory, as developed by economists and sociologists
Functionalism, as developed by Durkheim and later by Parsons
Conflict theory, as developed by Marx and later by Weber
Symbolic interactionism, as developed by Mead and later by Blumer

questions.prompt: A person who grew up in a poor family and becomes a physician has experienced:
choices: Intergenerational upward mobility, a higher position than that of parents
Intragenerational downward mobility, a fall in position within a lifetime
Horizontal mobility, a change in job without a change in social rank
Social reproduction, the transmission of the same position to children

questions.prompt: Bourdieu cultural capital refers to:
choices: Networks of relationships and trust that provide support and access
Official credentials granted by institutions after formal training
Money and property that can be converted into other forms of power
Knowledge, skills and habits that confer advantage in social settings

questions.prompt: A sociologist studies how a hospital ward constructs the meaning of a good patient through everyday talk between nurses and patients, and how labels shape the way people are treated. Which perspective is she using?
choices: Functionalism, which asks how each part supports social stability
Conflict theory, which asks how groups compete for power and resources
Symbolic interactionism, which asks how shared meaning arises in interaction
Demographic transition theory, which asks how birth and death rates change

questions.prompt: A 54-year-old man with diabetes lives in a neighborhood shaped decades earlier by lending practices that denied mortgages to residents based on race. The area has few grocery stores and clinics. Which concept most directly links history to his current health risk?
choices: Medicalization, the framing of an ordinary condition as a medical one
Institutional racism, with policies that shaped neighborhood resources
The sick role, with obligations to seek care that are placed on patients
Demographic transition, with a shift to low birth and death rates

questions.prompt: A health inequity is best defined as a difference in health that is:
choices: Limited to differences in the quality of care within a single hospital
Present between any two groups regardless of the cause of the difference
Unfair and avoidable, linked to social or economic disadvantage
Explained entirely by genetic variation that differs between populations

questions.prompt: The Whitehall studies of British civil servants found that mortality:
choices: Was highest in the top grades because of the demands of leadership
Differed only between the very poorest group and everyone else
Was similar across grades because all of the workers had stable jobs
Rose with each step down in employment grade, a social gradient

questions.prompt: Which term describes overlapping social identities that together produce experiences not captured by each identity alone?
choices: Intersectionality, a framework for overlapping identities and systems
Acculturation, the cultural change that results from sustained contact
Social reproduction, the passing of status from one generation to the next
Medicalization, the treatment of ordinary conditions as medical problems

questions.prompt: A clinic notes that Black women in its catchment area have higher rates of severe pregnancy complications than white women of the same insurance status. A trainee proposes that genetic differences explain the gap. Which response is most consistent with current evidence?
choices: Agree, since race corresponds to distinct biological subtypes of humans
Disagree, since racial gaps are tied to chronic stress, care quality and exposure
Agree, since the same insurance status removes every non-genetic explanation
Disagree, since pregnancy complications have no relationship to social factors

questions.prompt: A hospital adds screening for housing and food insecurity to its visits and connects patients to resources. In public health terms, this is best described as:
choices: An evaluation of internal validity in a randomized clinical trial
A strictly downstream measure that treats disease after it appears
An effort to address social needs, a step toward upstream causes
A measure of health literacy by means of a standardized test

questions.prompt: In the transtheoretical model, a patient who is not planning to change in the next six months is in:
choices: Preparation, with a plan to act in the very near future
Maintenance, with sustained change continuing for many months
Contemplation, with a serious consideration of change in the near future
Precontemplation, with no current intention to change the behavior

questions.prompt: Which technique asks a patient to restate the treatment plan in his own words to check understanding?
choices: Shaping, which reinforces successive approximations of a behavior
Implementation intentions, which are specific if-then plans for action
Teach-back, which confirms that information was understood correctly
Reflective listening, which mirrors the feelings expressed by the patient

questions.prompt: A core stance of motivational interviewing toward patient resistance is to:
choices: Confront the patient directly with the risks of continuing the behavior
Treat resistance as information and explore ambivalence with empathy
Offer a detailed action plan immediately to move the patient to action
Ask the patient to leave the visit until he has decided to change

questions.prompt: A 52-year-old man with hypertension says that he skips his pill because he feels fine and the pills make him tired, and he does not think his blood pressure is a serious problem. Which health belief model constructs are most directly involved?
choices: Low perceived severity and perceived barriers, since symptoms are absent and side effects exist
Perceived benefits only, since he believes that treatment is entirely useless
Social norms only, since his friends do not take medicine for high pressure
Cue to action and self-efficacy, since he lacks a reminder and confidence

questions.prompt: In a trial of a pain drug, participants given an inert tablet that they believe is an analgesic report meaningful pain relief, and some in the inert group report side effects. Which pair of effects is illustrated?
choices: Nocebo effect for the relief and placebo effect for the side effects
Hawthorne effect for the relief and social loafing for the side effects
Demand characteristics for the relief and extinction for the side effects
Placebo effect for the relief and nocebo effect for the side effects

questions.prompt: Which feature of an experiment most directly supports causal inference?
choices: Random assignment of participants to the conditions of the study
A high correlation between the independent and dependent variables
A survey instrument with questions that are worded very clearly
A large sample that is drawn from a single convenient setting

questions.prompt: A scale always reads 2 kilograms too heavy, giving the same value each time. This scale is:
choices: Neither reliable nor valid, because it does not report true weight
Reliable but not valid, because it is consistent but wrong
Valid but not reliable, because it is accurate but inconsistent
Both reliable and valid, because the error is perfectly systematic

questions.prompt: Which measure of central tendency is least affected by a few extremely high incomes in a sample?
choices: The standard deviation, which summarizes how widely values spread
The mean, which weights every value and shifts with outliers
The median, which is the middle value and resists outliers
The range, which is the gap between the highest and lowest value

questions.prompt: A study of 400 adults finds that those who sleep less than six hours also report more depressive symptoms (r = 0.35). A journalist writes that short sleep causes depression. Which critique is most valid?
choices: Random assignment was used so cause is established but cannot be generalized
The result has high internal validity but low reliability of measurement
The correlation is too small to be statistically significant at any sample size
The design cannot show direction or exclude confounds, so cause is not established

questions.prompt: A trial reports p = 0.03 for a drug that lowers a symptom score by an amount too small for patients to notice. Which interpretation is most accurate?
choices: The result is statistically significant but may lack practical importance
There is a 3 percent probability that the null hypothesis is true
The result proves the drug works because the p-value is below 0.05
The drug is clinically important because the result is statistically significant
